children: Vinay Bagri, Co-founder and CEO of Niyo explains, "we reduced losses through productivity improvements, particularly by using AI across customer service, operations, marketing, and product development"
Niyo, a travel-focused fintech platform, reported a 78 per cent increase in consolidated income to Rs 178 crore in FY26, while its losses declined 58 per cent to Rs 33 crore.

The company is expanding beyond its zero-forex markup cards into foreign exchange, remittances, travel bookings and credit products, while using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency.

In this exclusive interview, Vinay Bagri, Co-founder and CEO of Niyo, discusses the company’s revenue growth, cross-selling strategy, expansion into cross-border payments and plans to move towards EBITDA profitability.
Niyo’s consolidated income rose 78 per cent to Rs 178 crore in FY26, while losses fell 58 per cent to Rs 33 crore. What drove this improvement?

All three factors, customer growth, higher revenue per customer and operational efficiency—played a role. Our customer base grew during the year, and customers spent more abroad using Niyo cards with zero forex markup.

Consolidated income increased from Rs 100 crore to Rs 178 crore, outpacing customer growth. Newer products, including forex cash, outward remittances, multi-currency cards through our licensed subsidiary Kanji Forex, flights, hotels, insurance, experiences, and eSIMs, have increased revenue per customer. Our expanding forex branch network has also contributed to growth.

We reduced losses through productivity improvements, particularly by using AI across customer service, operations, marketing, and product development. Operating expenses grew 20 per cent to Rs 201 crore, despite the addition of more than 200 employees to expand the Kanji Forex business. EBITDA loss declined from Rs 77 crore to Rs 32 crore.

Our existing customers continue to use Niyo year after year, allowing us to generate more revenue without incurring additional acquisition costs. Customer acquisition has also become more efficient through Niyo Express, our assisted onboarding channel, which provides customers with a working card within 24 hours.
How is AI improving Niyo’s productivity, costs and customer experience?

AI has helped us grow without increasing costs at the same rate as revenue. Employee costs grew 17 per cent in FY26. In customer service, bot resolution rates increased by 4.7 to 8.5 percentage points year on year.

For forex cash orders, an AI relationship manager handles the post-order process, reducing verification time from around three hours to less than 30 minutes. Our in-app AI assistant, Aero, is being rolled out to address account and booking queries.

In marketing, AI-generated campaign creatives and landing-page testing helped increase new accounts from performance channels by 13 per cent while reducing paid acquisition costs by 11 per cent. Referral traffic from AI assistants, including ChatGPT and Gemini, grew 3.6 times over two quarters.

In product development and engineering, ten AI initiatives are live. AI tools help review product specifications, generate tests and enable product managers to build calculators and comparison tools without additional engineering support.

In compliance, 33 AI agents support our information security programme across more than 267 activities. Our approach is to have AI agents propose actions, with people approving them and every action being logged.
What are the main opportunities to increase revenue from existing customers?
Customer acquisition and monetisation are both growing. Our customers travel, study and spend abroad, creating opportunities to offer them multiple products.

Travel is a key area. The share of international card users who also book flights, hotels, insurance or eSIMs through Niyo increased by half in a year, while travel revenue more than doubled. Our paid membership, Niyo Premium, contributes to this growth, with members accounting for nearly half of all travel bookings.

Forex cash and remittances are other opportunities. Customers travelling abroad or supporting children studying overseas often need cash and transfer services alongside cards. Our forex cash business has an NPS of 74.
We also launched an unsecured zero-forex credit card in September, with around 50,000 people on the waitlist. Customers who do not qualify can use our savings-backed secured card.

Niyo Express, our assisted onboarding channel, also supports cross-selling. Customers acquired through this channel use more products than self-service users, and cross-sell revenue has grown severalfold in a year.
We expect customer acquisition and revenue per customer to continue growing together as customers use more of our products.
How do you expect Niyo’s revenue mix to change over the next three years?
Our co-branded zero-forex cards remain our largest revenue source. However, we expect forex cash, remittances, credit and travel to contribute a larger share over the coming years.

Forex cash and remittances are significant opportunities. Travel accounts for a substantial share of outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme. The Reserve Bank of India’s revised framework allows licensed providers to serve a wider range of personal remittance needs, including family maintenance and payments to tour operators, which can involve larger transaction values.
Our forex business is expanding, while RemitX is expected to add a nationwide branch and partner network.

Credit is another growth area. International card spending has been shifting towards credit following tax changes collected at source rules. Our unsecured zero-forex credit card is intended to address this demand while bringing domestic spending onto the platform.

Travel bookings and Niyo Premium memberships are also expected to contribute, as they generate revenue and increase customer engagement. Over time, we expect cards to remain an important business while newer products become additional sources of revenue.
How will the GIFT City entity and proposed RemitX acquisition support Niyo’s cross-border payments business?
The two developments, alongside our forex licence, are intended to expand our ability to serve customers digitally, through physical locations and across borders.

We have established Finnew Global Solutions IFSC Private Limited in GIFT City, which has received approval as a Payment Service Provider under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA). This allows us to develop cross-border payment flows through an international financial centre and in foreign currencies. It could create new revenue streams and reduce our reliance on intermediaries, improving margins on existing transactions.

We have also signed a definitive agreement to acquire the forex business of Capital India Finance Limited, which operates under the RemitX brand. The business has more than 30 branches across 14 states, over 2,500 partners among travel agents, overseas education consultants and corporates, and a team of more than 200 employees.

Niyo's digital distribution model and RemitX's branch-based and partner-led network are expected to complement each other. In cross-border payments, many customer decisions still begin with a conversation at a branch or with an education consultant. The acquisition would give us access to both digital and physical distribution channels.

In August, the Reserve Bank of India granted our subsidiary Kanji Forex a perpetual AD-II licence with a wider scope. RemitX's distribution network would help us serve customers across education, travel, family maintenance and corporate payments.

Following completion of the acquisition, our physical footprint is expected to exceed 40 locations, moving us closer to our target of 50 branches. Our ambition is to secure a 10-15 per cent share of India's cross-border market.
What milestones will help Niyo achieve EBITDA profitability while maintaining annual growth of more than 50 per cent?
We aim to maintain annual growth of more than 50 per cent while working towards becoming EBITDA-positive. FY26 demonstrated that we could grow revenue while significantly reducing our EBITDA loss.

Our priorities include increasing revenue from existing customers, scaling the unsecured credit card, completing and integrating RemitX, and expanding travel, Premium memberships, forex cash and remittances. These products can generate additional revenue from customers we have already acquired, limiting incremental acquisition costs.

We will also continue to keep costs growing more slowly than revenue, with AI contributing to operational efficiency. Our existing customer base provides an opportunity to grow revenue while keeping acquisition costs relatively stable.

Investment decisions will depend on returns. Niyo Express costs more to operate than self-service onboarding, but its customers activate faster, stay longer and use more products, allowing the channel to cover its costs. We apply a similar approach to technology and expansion.
We ended FY26 with a strong balance sheet and established banking partnerships, which provide flexibility to continue investing in products and technology while working towards profitability.
Kalyan Shobhana
